script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. Friday — here is your QQQ recap. The portfolio closed one point zero eight percent up on the session. A volatile end to July, with sharp divergence across the major technology names.

Amazon surged more than fifteen percent in Friday's session. Apple fell nearly eight. One company confirmed the AI infrastructure thesis. The other exposed just how fragile supply chains remain for hardware makers leaning on the same boom.

The Nasdaq finished higher on Friday despite the split verdict across technology. Amazon's earnings-driven rally helped lift the index, offsetting pressure from Apple's steep decline. The Dow also closed in positive territory. Yields spiked during the session, adding a layer of complexity to what was otherwise a strong close for cloud-exposed names.

The headline of Friday's session belongs to Amazon. Shares soared fifteen point three two percent after the company reported strong cloud sales growth that reinforced investor confidence in its artificial intelligence spending commitments. Amazon Web Services delivered, and the market responded decisively. Analysts pointed to the company's massive AI infrastructure bets as the core driver of the move. Maxim Group's Tom Forte noted that even with negative free cash flow in the second quarter, the market is looking through near-term capital intensity toward long-term cloud compute capacity. For this portfolio, where Amazon represents four point zero eight percent of holdings, Friday's move was a meaningful contributor to the overall session gain.

Nvidia was up two point nine three percent on Friday. The AI trade remains central to Nvidia's story, and commentary from Tusk Ventures founder Bradley Tusk reinforced that dynamic — framing the broader artificial intelligence investment narrative as a blend of perception and reality. The key question heading into next week is whether that perception continues to be validated by hardware demand data.

Apple was down seven point three five percent on the session. The drop followed a disappointing forecast that showed the iPhone maker struggling to secure enough components as the AI-driven data center boom strains global supply chains. The decline, at one point reaching ten percent intraday, was significant enough to briefly threaten Apple's position as the world's most valuable company, with Reuters reporting nearly five hundred billion dollars in market capitalization at risk. For a position representing six point eight percent of this portfolio, that is a material drag. The component supply constraint story will be the key watch item going into next week.

Alphabet was up six point seven three percent on Friday. The move comes against a backdrop where cloud-exposed names broadly benefited from Amazon's results. There was no Alphabet-specific catalyst, but the company's positioning in AI infrastructure kept it in favor on a day that rewarded cloud compute exposure.

Micron was down five point nine zero percent on Friday. The session was a whipsaw — Micron had surged approximately eighteen percent on Thursday, and Friday brought profit-taking. Analysts noted that higher interest rates and repositioning outweighed the clear signal from Amazon's results that cloud and device companies need increasing quantities of memory chips. Wall Street continues to debate the durability of Micron's rebound.

Microsoft was up three point zero two percent. The session's broad AI infrastructure enthusiasm extended to Microsoft, consistent with its deep Azure and artificial intelligence integration story. Turning to Advanced Micro Devices, the stock was down one point nine zero percent on Friday, a modest pullback with no specific catalyst — likely sympathy pressure from the mixed semiconductor session. Over at Tesla, shares were up zero point seven six percent — a quiet close, with no major news driving the move. Meanwhile, Intel was down one point zero two percent, continuing to lag its semiconductor peers in a session that rewarded AI infrastructure over legacy chip exposure.

On the secondary side, Meta Platforms deserves a mention — up three point two eight percent on Friday, benefiting from the same AI and digital advertising tailwinds that lifted Alphabet. Broadcom finished up zero point three seven percent. Sandisk was down five point zero nine percent, tracking the broader memory sector weakness alongside Micron.

Three data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, SpaceX delivers its first quarterly earnings results since going public — the company's AI business ambitions will be under particular scrutiny, with analysts noting that the rocket launch count is visible, but the AI strategy is not. Second, watch for any Federal Reserve commentary following Friday's yield spike — any shift in rate expectations will matter for the growth-heavy names in this portfolio. Third, monitor semiconductor supply chain data and any analyst revisions following Apple's component warning — downstream effects on Advanced Micro Devices and Intel are worth tracking closely.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. The SpaceX earnings report and continued reaction to Apple's supply chain warning will set the tone early in the week ahead.
